lines.trans: I beg you, the main thing in a restaurant is management!
Any fool can whip up food, even I can.
Any fool can whip something up, but try to actually cook!
Believe me, I know what I am talking about!
What did you do there, just boil eggs?

lines.trans: Let's you and I make a bet right now!
Rabbit baked under almond sauce with rosemary and truffles.
Try to cook a dish like that yourself by evening!
When you die, not a single germ will be left on you.
I hope I do not die from your dish!
I promise you, old pal, the dish will be excellent!
Great, then it is a deal, shake on it!

examples.text: Оно греет и влюблённую пару, и одинокого парня.
examples.trans: It warms both a couple in love and a lonely guy.

examples.text: Одинокого парня, который уже забыл, что такое солнце.
examples.trans: A lonely guy who has already forgotten what the sun is.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Попробуй сам приготовить такое блюдо к вечеру!
examples.trans: Try to cook a dish like that yourself by evening!

examples.text: Ты поспорил, что за вечер научишься готовить это блюдо?
examples.trans: You bet that in one evening you would learn to cook this dish?

examples.text: Дима, до вечера это совершенно невозможно!
examples.trans: Dima, before evening that is completely impossible!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Оно греет и влюблённую пару, и одинокого парня.
examples.trans: It warms both a couple in love and a lonely guy.

examples.text: Одинокого парня, который уже забыл, что такое солнце.
examples.trans: A lonely guy who has already forgotten what the sun is.

examples.text: Когда умрёшь, на тебе ни одного микроба не останется.
examples.trans: When you die, not a single germ will be left on you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мереть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to die', paired with 'умирать'.

examples.text: Она умерла в прошлом году.
examples.trans: She died last year.

examples.text: Он умер очень старым.
examples.trans: He died very old.

examples.text: Но она всё равно умерла.
examples.trans: But she died anyway.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как говорил один мудрец, солнце светит всем одинаково.
examples.trans: As one wise man said, the sun shines equally on everyone.

examples.text: Теперь весь ресторан полностью на мне.
examples.trans: Now the entire restaurant is completely on my shoulders.

examples.text: По поводу ресторана я тебе уже говорил, Дима.
examples.trans: I already told you about the restaurant, Dima.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not even, nor', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да ничего не рухнет, главное в ресторане что?
examples.trans: Nothing will collapse, what is the main thing in a restaurant?

examples.text: Я тебя умоляю, главное в ресторане — управление!
examples.trans: I beg you, the main thing in a restaurant is management!

examples.text: Когда умрёшь, на тебе ни одного микроба не останется.
examples.trans: When you die, not a single germ will be left on you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'alone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как говорил один мудрец, солнце светит всем одинаково.
examples.trans: As one wise man said, the sun shines equally on everyone.

examples.text: Оно греет и влюблённую пару, и одинокого парня.
examples.trans: It warms both a couple in love and a lonely guy.

examples.text: Одинокого парня, который уже забыл, что такое солнце.
examples.trans: A lonely guy who has already forgotten what the sun is.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'microbe / germ' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Когда умрёшь, на тебе ни одного микроба не останется.
examples.trans: When you die, not a single germ will be left on you.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть микроб.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always microbe.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь весь ресторан полностью на мне.
examples.trans: Now the entire restaurant is completely on my shoulders.

examples.text: Продай его нам, одной проблемой меньше станет.
examples.trans: Sell it to us, and you will have one less problem.

examples.text: Если я уйду, здесь всё рухнет без меня!
examples.trans: If I leave, everything here will collapse without me!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'remains', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: There's nothing left.

examples.text: Я останусь дома.
examples.trans: I'll stay at home.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hope', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, вы меня поняли.
examples.trans: I hope you understood me.

examples.text: Я надеюсь. Идите, действуйте быстрее!
examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

examples.text: Я надеюсь.
examples.trans: I hope so.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Одинокого парня, который уже забыл, что такое солнце.
examples.trans: A lonely guy who has already forgotten what the sun is.

examples.text: Двадцать четыре часа в сутки работаю как раб.
examples.trans: I work twenty-four hours a day like a slave.

examples.text: Состряпать может любой дурак, а ты попробуй приготовить!
examples.trans: Any fool can whip something up, but try to actually cook!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Надеюсь, я умру не от твоего блюда!
examples.trans: I hope I do not die from your dish!

examples.text: Значит, она просто удалила твой номер.
examples.trans: That means she simply deleted your number.

examples.text: Она удалила твой номер.
examples.trans: She deleted your number.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ещать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'promise', paired with 'пообещать'.

examples.text: Я тебе обещаю, старик, блюдо будет отличное!
examples.trans: I promise you, old pal, the dish will be excellent!

examples.text: Я вам обещаю.
examples.trans: I promise you.

examples.text: Ты обещал!
examples.trans: You promised!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тарик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'old man' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я тебе обещаю, старик, блюдо будет отличное!
examples.trans: I promise you, old pal, the dish will be excellent!

examples.text: Старая заначка под подкладку куртки провалилась!
examples.trans: An old stash slipped under the lining of the jacket!

examples.text: Выигранный спор, старая заначка и премии!
examples.trans: The bet you won, the old stash, and the bonuses!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: Я просто хочу быть таким же крутым, как ты!
examples.trans: I just want to be as cool as you!

examples.text: Я думаю, может быть, специи не свежие были?
examples.trans: I think maybe the spices were not fresh?

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Я тебе обещаю, старик, блюдо будет отличное!
examples.trans: I promise you, old pal, the dish will be excellent!

examples.text: Отлично, тогда договорились, по рукам!
examples.trans: Great, then it is a deal, shake on it!

examples.text: Отлично, теперь денег становится всё больше!
examples.trans: Great, now the pile of money is getting bigger and bigger!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я тебе обещаю, старик, блюдо будет отличное!
examples.trans: I promise you, old pal, the dish will be excellent!

examples.text: Отлично, тогда договорились, по рукам!
examples.trans: Great, then it is a deal, shake on it!

examples.text: Отлично, теперь денег становится всё больше!
examples.trans: Great, now the pile of money is getting bigger and bigger!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Отлично, тогда договорились, по рукам!
examples.trans: Great, then it is a deal, shake on it!

examples.text: Ведь все девчонки всегда этого хотят!
examples.trans: After all, all girls always want that!

examples.text: Ты же сам видишь, она этого хочет.
examples.trans: You see for yourself that she wants this.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'agreed, deal', paired with 'договариваться'.

examples.text: Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы договорились.
examples.trans: We've agreed.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'according to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Отлично, тогда договорились, по рукам!
examples.trans: Great, then it is a deal, shake on it!

examples.text: Дай руку.
examples.trans: Give me your hand.
